issues.detail: Covers mainly the happy path with little troubleshooting guidance (e.g., failed startup, webhook/trigger failures, upgrades, backups of Postgres, or flow run errors).

scenarios.name: selfhost-compose-with-secrets
scenarios.rationale: Both provide compose files with activepieces, postgres and redis from ghcr.io, openssl-generated secrets, and chmod 600 .env. A explicitly warns never to rotate either the encryption key or the JWT secret and says to keep .env out of git. B warns only about the encryption key, never mentions the JWT secret, and doesn't say to keep secrets out of version control. B is much more thorough on production hardening, which pulls the scores closer together despite those two rubric gaps.

scenarios.name: shopify-large-order-slack-flow
scenarios.rationale: A follows the rubric structure exactly (Shopify New Order trigger, Code step returning total and overThreshold, Branch on overThreshold, Slack Send Message to Channel #orders) with an async function returning an object; B gives the primary path as a total_price branch without a Code step, and its Code step is optional and returns only total with no overThreshold boolean.

scenarios.name: custom-piece-and-production-urls
scenarios.rationale: A covers all rubric points: createPiece with PieceAuth.SecretText, triggers/actions arrays, `npx activepieces pieces create`, and both AP_API_URL and AP_FRONTEND_URL set to the HTTPS domain with the OAuth/webhook breakage warning; B uses a different scaffold command (`npm run cli pieces create`) and omits AP_API_URL (offering AP_WEBHOOK_URL instead), missing a key rubric item despite extensive detail.
